harness_failures_resolved: Initial temporary-directory access failures were avoided by selecting an owned writable TEMP.

The first full unit run had 1582 passes, 1077 passing subtests, eight skips and one outside-repository fixture failure because TEMP was inside the worktree. Moving TEMP outside the checkout restored the negative fixture; its 11 methods and 14 subtests passed.
First new Chromium run had a test-only link hidden under the app shell; positioned the synthetic link and reran both connected tests successfully.
limitations: No full security/authentication or all-category retention acceptance; parent issues remain open and matrices are unchanged.
An ancestry check followed by path-based unlink does not provide atomic protection against a hostile filesystem swap between the final check and deletion.
Windows local tests use synthetic SQLite and native temporary directory links; PostgreSQL/Redis/Compose local full-stack checks NOT_RUN.
Eight Linux-launcher unit cases require Linux and remain skipped on the Windows host; required exact-head hosted checks pending.
Real applications, live provider inference, credential access and unrelated host changes were not performed.
